intro:
The best self propelled lawn mower for most flat-to-rolling yards up to about half an acre is the Toro Recycler 22-Inch Personal Pace SmartStow, because its drive follows your walking speed with no dial to fiddle with. If your lawn slopes or you want to drop gas, the rear-wheel-drive EGO Power+ LM2135SP is the stronger pick.

Buying a self-propelled mower is really buying a drive system. Engine size and deck width get the attention, but whether you finish the lawn tired or fresh depends on which wheels are powered, how the speed is set and whether the mower keeps traction on a slope as the bag fills. This guide ranks six gas and battery models, then answers the drive, sizing, runtime and repair questions owners search for.
quickAnswer: Buy the Toro Recycler 22-Inch Personal Pace for most yards, the EGO LM2135SP for slopes or battery power, and the 30-inch Toro TimeMaster for half to three quarters of an acre. On flat lots and tighter budgets, the Craftsman M275 and Troy-Bilt TB230 are the simple gas choices, and the Ryobi 40V HP Brushless is the value battery pick.

sections.heading: Best Self Propelled Lawn Mowers: The Short Answer
sections.body:
The **Toro Recycler 22-Inch Personal Pace SmartStow** is the best self-propelled mower for most yards. The **EGO Power+ LM2135SP** is the best battery choice and the better mower on slopes, thanks to rear-wheel drive.

| Mower | Best for | Key spec |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Toro Recycler 22-Inch Personal Pace SmartStow | Most yards to about 1/2 acre | Gas, front drive, 22 in. steel deck |
| EGO Power+ LM2135SP | Sloped lots around 1/4 acre, going battery | 56V, rear drive, 21 in. Select Cut deck |
| Toro TimeMaster 30-Inch | 1/2 to 3/4 acre with gates or terraces | Gas, rear drive, 30 in. two-blade deck |
| Craftsman M275 | Budget gas on flat yards | Front drive, single speed, 21 in. 3-in-1 |
| Ryobi 40V HP Brushless 21-Inch | Flat lots to 1/4 acre, Ryobi 40V owners | 40V, front drive, variable speed |
| Troy-Bilt TB230 | Simple gas mower for flat lots to 1/3 acre | Front drive, single speed, high rear wheels |

Choose the drive layout first: rear-wheel drive for any slope or regular bagging, front-wheel drive for flat lots with lots of turns. Then let your actual grass area decide gas or battery.

sections.heading: The 6 Best Self Propelled Lawn Mowers in 2026, Ranked
sections.body:
Each pick rests on published manufacturer specifications (drive type, deck size, engine or battery rating and warranty), the reach of dealer and parts networks, and patterns in owner feedback. None of these mowers was put through hands-on or lab trials for this guide; the text says when a claim comes from a spec sheet or from owners.

### Best Overall: Toro Recycler 22-Inch Personal Pace SmartStow
This Toro leads because of its Personal Pace drive. There is no speed lever or dial; the mower senses how firmly you push the handle, slowing as you ease up at a bed edge and speeding up on a long straight run. In owner reviews, this drive draws fewer complaints than any other system in the price range. The 22-inch steel deck is an inch wider than most, saving a few passes on a typical suburban lot, and the recycling deck is shaped to keep clippings airborne long enough to chop them fine. SmartStow means you can tip it up onto its rear and park it vertically with fuel and oil still inside, a real help when the garage only fits one car. The weakness is front-wheel drive: on a steep bank with the bag loaded, the front wheels lose weight and slip. On flat to gently rolling ground up to about half an acre, that never comes up.

**Pros:** Personal Pace drive; 22-inch recycling deck; stores upright; wide parts network.
**Cons:** Front drive slips uphill with a full bag; steel deck needs to stay clean.

[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Toro+Recycler+22+inch+Personal+Pace+SmartStow&tag=sktiger-20)

### Top Battery Pick: EGO Power+ LM2135SP 21-Inch Select Cut
The LM2135SP pairs EGO's 56-volt platform with rear-wheel drive, the right layout for anyone who mows uphill. As you climb and as the bag fills, weight moves onto the rear wheels, so they keep biting where front-drive mowers spin. Select Cut mounts a pair of blades on a single spindle, and you can change the bottom blade to a mulching or high-lift style as the season changes. Owners say it handles dense spring growth cleanly as long as they drop the speed and lift the cutting height one setting. Runtime is the trade-off: it drops in long, damp growth, so plan on a second battery for lawns larger than about a third of an acre. Otherwise ownership is easy, with no fuel, oil, spark plug or winterizing. The steel-framed polymer deck will not rust, and the mower folds compactly for storage.

**Pros:** Rear drive grips on slopes; Select Cut blades; no engine upkeep; shares EGO 56V batteries.
**Cons:** Runtime falls in tall, wet grass; spare batteries are expensive.

[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=EGO+LM2135SP&tag=sktiger-20)

### Best for Large Yards: Toro TimeMaster 30-Inch Personal Pace
The TimeMaster fills the gap between a 21-inch walk-behind and a riding mower. Plenty of lots sit between half and three quarters of an acre, where a 21-inch deck means a long walk but a lawn tractor is too much machine or will not fit through the side gate. The 30-inch deck cuts roughly 40 percent more per pass than a 21-inch, and Toro puts two blades under it to keep the cut even across the width. Drive is rear-wheel with the same Personal Pace handle as the Recycler, which matters on a mower this heavy, since you want the drive, not your arms, doing the climbing. The handle folds for storage. The drawbacks are weight, a wider turning effort around trees and beds, and a price close to an entry lawn tractor. On terraces, gated yards and tight corners it is the practical choice.

**Pros:** 30-inch two-blade deck; rear drive with Personal Pace; fits through gates a rider cannot.
**Cons:** Heavy and harder to turn; costs about as much as an entry rider.

[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Toro+TimeMaster+30+inch&tag=sktiger-20)

### Top Budget Gas: Craftsman M275 21-Inch
The M275 is the classic starter self-propelled: a 21-inch steel deck, a mainstream small engine, front-wheel drive and a 3-in-1 setup for bagging, mulching or side discharge. Its drive runs at a single fixed pace: fine for a brisk walker on flat ground, a little pushy for anyone who likes to stroll. Front drive makes it easy to tip up and pivot around beds, but it is the wrong layout for a steep front bank. In return you get a price well under the premium brands and a mower any small-engine shop can fix, with parts and blades stocked at big-box stores. Owners commonly report reliable starts when fuel is kept fresh and the air filter is changed each season. Treat it as a five-to-eight-year mower with basic care, and it is fair value.

**Pros:** Low price; 3-in-1 deck; simple, serviceable drive; easy parts.
**Cons:** Single speed; struggles on steep banks; lighter components.

[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Craftsman+M275&tag=sktiger-20)

### Top Value Battery: Ryobi 40V HP Brushless 21-Inch
Ryobi's HP Brushless self-propelled mower is the budget-friendly way into battery mowing. It has a 21-inch deck, a brushless motor and a variable-speed drive, and it runs on the same 40V batteries as Ryobi's trimmers and blowers, so many buyers already own a spare. That is a real saving, since an extra large-capacity pack from any maker is a big fraction of what the mower costs. Many kits include dual battery ports for longer runtime. Drive is front-wheel, so the usual caution about slopes and a heavy bag applies. Owners with level yards of a quarter acre or less generally say one charge covers a normal weekly cut. Build quality is lighter than EGO's, and some owners notice handle flex, but it folds easily and buying through Home Depot simplifies returns and warranty claims.

**Pros:** Brushless motor and variable speed; shared 40V batteries; push-button start.
**Cons:** Front drive weaker on slopes; plastic parts feel less robust.

[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Ryobi+40V+HP+Brushless+self+propelled+mower&tag=sktiger-20)

### Best Simple Gas Mower: Troy-Bilt TB230 21-Inch
The TB230 earns its spot by being plain. You get a 21-inch steel deck, front wheels driven at one speed, and oversized back wheels that ride over bumps instead of shaving the humps bare. With no speed dial and no complicated handle linkage, it appeals to owners who want to keep a mower a long time and do their own maintenance. Like the Craftsman, it turns easily around beds and loses grip on steep banks. Owners commonly describe it as a dependable mower once they learn to keep the drive cable adjusted and the deck scraped. It usually costs about the same as the M275, so the choice often comes down to which store is closer. For level ground up to a third of an acre, you will be fine with either.

**Pros:** Few parts to fail; high rear wheels; 3-in-1 deck; low price.
**Cons:** Single speed; not suited to steep slopes.

[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Troy-Bilt+TB230&tag=sktiger-20)

sections.heading: Front, Rear or All-Wheel Drive: Which Self Propelled Mower Is Best?
sections.body:
Rear-wheel drive is the right choice for sloped yards and anyone who bags clippings; front-wheel drive suits flat lots with lots of turns. Settle the drive layout before you compare engines, batteries or decks.

| Drive layout | Best ground | Weak spot | Price tier |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Front-wheel | Flat lots with many turns | Climbing with a full bag | Lowest |
| Rear-wheel | Slopes, bagging, thick grass | Pivots take more effort | Middle |
| All-wheel | Steep or uneven terrain | Price and weight | Highest |

### When is front-wheel drive enough?
It is the most common and cheapest layout. You can press down on the handle, lift the drive wheels and spin the mower on its rear wheels, which makes it nimble around trees and beds. Uphill, or as the rear bag fills, weight comes off the front wheels and they slip.

### Why does rear-wheel drive grip better?
It puts the power under the weight. Climbing and bagging press the rear wheels harder into the turf. Turns take slightly more effort, but most owners adapt within a couple of mows.

### Is all-wheel drive worth it?
Only on genuinely steep, uneven or soggy ground. A typical suburban yard is better served by spending the money on a good rear-drive mower.

sections.heading: Single Speed, Variable Speed or Personal Pace: Which Is Easiest?
sections.body:
Of the three systems, a handle that senses your pace is the least work, a speed dial is a fair compromise, and one fixed speed suits you only if it happens to match how you walk.

### Is single speed a deal-breaker?
Not always. On an open lot with a steady walker, the fixed speed simply becomes your pace. The trouble is a mismatch: long-legged owners tend to find cheap drives sluggish, and smaller or older owners feel dragged along. Try it in the store if you can.

### What do dials and pace-sensing handles add?
A dial lets you pick a pace and hold it, which helps in thick grass where slowing gives the blade time to cut. A pace-sensing handle, such as Toro's Personal Pace, follows you automatically, slowing when you slow around obstacles. Anyone with arthritis or a weak grip should weigh that heavily, since budget drive levers often need a firm squeeze.

### How do battery mowers handle speed?
Electronically, which usually feels smooth and can offer a wider range than belt-driven gas drives. Whatever the system, slow down in tall growth. Rushing through overgrown grass is the top cause of a ragged cut, a clogged chute and a flat battery.

sections.heading: Should You Buy a Gas or Battery Self Propelled Mower?
sections.body:
Battery is usually the smarter purchase for level lawns below roughly a third of an acre. Pick gas when the lawn is bigger, hillier or regularly left to grow long.

### Where does battery win?
A current 21-inch battery mower with a brushless motor cuts cleanly, starts with a button, runs far quieter and needs almost no routine maintenance: no oil, no carburetor, no fuel can. If your lawn fits within real-world runtime, it is simply less work to own, and the lack of noise and fumes matters if you mow near a patio or open windows.

### Where does gas still win?
Runtime and steady power under load. A single fill-up finishes a big lawn in one go, and the engine keeps its power through heavy, damp growth instead of tapering off. The best self propelled gas lawn mowers, like the Toro Recycler and TimeMaster, remain the practical answer past half an acre. For deeper engine care, see our [gas lawn mower guide](/best-gas-lawn-mowers/).

### Which costs less to own?
Closer than the price tags suggest. Gas needs oil, a plug, an air filter and stabilizer every year plus an occasional carburetor cleaning. Battery skips all that, but packs slowly lose capacity and a replacement high-capacity battery costs a big share of the mower. Owning batteries from the same tool line tips the math toward battery.

### What about self-driving robot mowers?
Robotic mowers are a separate category that runs on a schedule without you. They suit small to mid-size, well-defined lawns and cost more up front; a self-propelled walk-behind is still the simpler, cheaper choice for most yards.

sections.heading: What Size Self Propelled Mower Do You Need for Your Yard?
sections.body:
Match the deck to the grass, not the lot. A quarter acre of turf takes a 21-inch self-propelled roughly 30 to 45 minutes; past half an acre a 30-inch walk-behind starts paying for itself; and once open lawn tops three quarters of an acre, a rider or [zero turn mower](/best-zero-turn-mower/) is usually the better tool.

| Grass area | 21-inch mowing time | Better tool |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Up to 1/4 acre | 30 to 45 min | Any 21-inch, battery shines |
| 1/4 to 1/2 acre | 45 to 75 min | Strong 21 or 22-inch, gas or two batteries |
| 1/2 to 3/4 acre | 75+ min | 30-inch walk-behind |
| Over 3/4 acre open lawn | Long | Rider or zero-turn |

### How do you measure your grass?
Lot size overstates it. A half-acre lot with a house, driveway, patio and beds may hold a quarter acre of lawn. Pace it out or use a satellite map tool, and compare that figure, not the deed, with battery runtime and deck width.

### Is a wider deck worth it?
A 22-inch deck adds a little per pass. A 30-inch adds a lot but makes the mower heavy and harder to steer among beds and trees, so save it for large, open lawns.

### Do deck material and blades matter?
Steel decks last if kept clean and dry; cast aluminum and polymer decks do not rust. Cut quality comes from sharp blades and deck shape, and stacked or dual blades leave finer mulch.

sections.heading: Why Is My Self Propelled Mower Not Pulling, and How Do You Fix It?
sections.body:
Three culprits cover most cases, and you can fix each one in the driveway for little money: a cable that has stretched, a belt that has gone shiny and slick, or clippings jammed into the wheel gears. Before touching anything, pull the spark plug wire on a gas mower or remove the battery, and wait for the blade to stop.

### Start with the drive cable
Most mowers have a barrel adjuster or nut near the handle or transmission. A few turns take up slack and restore full engagement. Make it part of your spring start-up routine.

### Check the belt next
Remove the belt cover and look for glazing, cracks or looseness. Belts are an inexpensive wear part every few seasons on a regularly used mower, so replacing one is routine.

### Clear packed grass from the wheels
Clippings build up around the drive wheels, pinion gears and transmission pulley and act like a brake. Once a season, pull the wheels, clean the gear teeth and confirm the small pawls inside each wheel move freely. If the plastic gear teeth are rounded off, replacements are cheap and easy to fit.

### What do battery mowers need?
No belt or cable, but the wheels and gears still need cleaning, and the battery should spend winter indoors at a moderate charge.

### What is the most reliable self propelled mower?
The simplest drives fail least. Single-speed front-drive mowers like the Troy-Bilt TB230 have few parts to wear, and well-supported models like the Toro Recycler have easy parts access. Reliability comes mostly from a tensioned cable, clean wheels, fresh fuel and a sharp blade.

sections.heading: Should You Bag, Mulch or Side-Discharge, and How Much Should You Spend?
sections.body:
Mulch a regularly mown lawn, bag when you want a clean finish or leaves are down, and side-discharge when the grass has run away from you.

### How does bagging affect the drive?
A filling bag adds weight behind the rear axle. That helps a rear-drive mower and hurts a front-drive one, which is why regular baggers on any slope should buy rear-wheel drive. A rigid-frame bag with a top handle is easier to empty than a floppy cloth sack.

### When does mulching work best?
On healthy turf mown on schedule, taking no more than about a third of the blade height. Long grass mulches into wet clumps that smother the lawn.

### When should you side-discharge?
After a wet week or a trip. Raise the deck, make a first pass with the chute, then mow lower with the mulch plug a few days later. Forcing overgrown grass through a bag in one pass overworks drive belts.

### How much should you spend?
Retail pricing falls into three tiers. Entry gas models bring front drive, often a single speed and a steel deck. The middle tier, where most buyers belong, adds rear drive or pace-sensing speed, better decks and longer warranties. Premium walk-behinds add aluminum decks, all-wheel drive, 30-inch decks or large battery packs; when a 30-inch model approaches the price of an entry rider, compare the two. Budget for a second battery, a spare blade and a [string trimmer](/best-weed-eater/) for the edges.

mistakes.title: Choosing front-wheel drive for a hilly lawn
mistakes.body: Pushing uphill shifts weight off the front wheels, and a filling bag makes the slipping worse. Any real grade on your property is a reason to choose rear or all-wheel drive. Skip that and you will be muscling a powered mower up the same hill every weekend.

mistakes.title: Trusting the runtime printed on the battery box
mistakes.body: Box runtimes assume ideal conditions, and long, damp or dense grass cuts them sharply. Work out your real turf area, hold it against the rated coverage without rounding in your favor, and buy a spare pack if the numbers are tight. Running flat mid-lawn is the top battery-mower complaint.

mistakes.title: Writing off the drive before adjusting the cable
mistakes.body: A weak drive usually means a stretched cable, not a dead transmission. Most mowers have a simple adjuster near the handle or transmission that restores full engagement in a minute. Check it every spring before pricing a new transmission or a new mower.

mistakes.title: Racing through tall grass at full speed
mistakes.body: Hurrying through long grass tears the tips, plugs the bag and chute, and empties a battery fast. Lift the cutting height, back off the speed and overlap more on each pass. The job still ends sooner, because you are not stopping every few rows to dig out a clog.

mistakes.title: Paying for a drive a small lawn does not need
mistakes.body: For a level patch of a few thousand square feet, a powered drive mostly brings extra weight, extra cost and extra parts to fail. A light push mower or compact battery mower handles the job and is easier to store. Spend the savings on a spare blade.

faqs.q: What is the best self propelled lawn mower?
faqs.a: The Toro Recycler 22-Inch Personal Pace SmartStow is the best self propelled lawn mower for most flat-to-rolling yards up to about half an acre, thanks to its speed-sensing drive and good mulching deck. On slopes, or if you want battery power, the rear-wheel-drive EGO LM2135SP is the stronger choice.

faqs.q: What are the best self propelled gas lawn mowers?
faqs.a: The Toro Recycler 22-Inch Personal Pace is the best gas self-propelled mower for most yards, and the Toro TimeMaster 30-Inch is the pick for half to three quarters of an acre. On flat lots and tighter budgets, the Craftsman M275 and Troy-Bilt TB230 are simple, serviceable gas choices with 21-inch 3-in-1 decks.

faqs.q: Is rear-wheel drive better than front-wheel drive on a mower?
faqs.a: On slopes and when bagging, yes. Going uphill or carrying a heavy bag loads the back wheels, which helps a rear-drive mower bite and leaves a front-drive one scrabbling. Front-wheel drive turns more easily because you can lift the drive wheels and pivot, so it suits flat lots full of obstacles.

faqs.q: Can a battery self propelled mower handle half an acre?
faqs.a: A few can, though nearly always with a big pack or a spare. Box runtimes assume ideal conditions, and dense or damp grass shortens them. If you really have half an acre of grass, choose a two-battery kit or a mower that holds two packs at once. Below a quarter acre, a single quality pack usually gets the job done.

faqs.q: How long does a self propelled lawn mower last?
faqs.a: A well-maintained gas self-propelled from a major brand typically gives eight to ten seasons, and aluminum-deck premium models often go further. Budget for a new drive belt and cable now and then; they are wear items. Battery mowers have fewer wear parts, but packs slowly lose capacity over several years.

faqs.q: Why does my self propelled mower struggle going uphill?
faqs.a: The usual suspects are a slack drive cable, a slick worn belt, clippings jammed into the wheel gears, or simply front drive losing traction as the load shifts rearward. Adjust the cable first, then clean the wheels and inspect the belt. If the mower is front drive and the bank is steep, the layout itself is the limit.

faqs.q: Is a self propelled mower worth it for a small lawn?
faqs.a: Often not. A small level yard is better served by a lightweight push or compact battery model, which is cheaper, easier to tuck away and simpler mechanically. A powered drive earns its cost on hills, for regular bagging, or when a single mow runs long enough that pushing becomes a chore.

bottomLine: Decide the drive before anything else: rear-wheel drive for any lawn that slopes or gets bagged, front-wheel drive for flat lots full of turns. After that, the square footage of grass you really cut, and how often it gets away from you, picks gas or battery. The Toro Recycler 22-Inch Personal Pace and the EGO LM2135SP are the best self propelled lawn mowers for most yards, the Toro TimeMaster covers bigger lots, and the Craftsman M275, Troy-Bilt TB230 and Ryobi 40V HP handle flat ground on a budget. Keep the drive cable tensioned, the wheels clean and the blade sharp, and any of them can give you close to a decade of easy mowing.
